title: Article Eater Theory Hierarchy
description: Defines the multi-tier explanatory structure that organises all theoretical knowledge in the system.

T1.name: Framework Theories
T1.definition: Neurally grounded, cross-domain frameworks. Every architectural effect must operate through one or more of these. Each satisfies three criteria: (1) mechanistic specificity — connects to neural implementation, (2) cross-domain generativity — predictions across multiple domains, (3) convergent multi-method support — fMRI, EEG, lesion, computational, behavioral evidence.

T1.5.name: Domain Theories
T1.5.definition: Phenomenological organizing schemas that describe effects within a domain. They are EXPLAINED BY Tier 1 frameworks, not explanatory themselves. Each has a published author, established constructs, and formal reduction mappings showing how T1 mechanisms account for the domain theory's constructs. Useful labels, but not fundamental mechanisms.
T1.5.relationship_to_T1: Reduced to T1 frameworks via explicit coverage fractions and irreducible residuals.

Molecule.name: Molecules
Molecule.definition: Compositional units that package multiple T2 templates into coherent effect bundles. A molecule defines HOW a set of mechanism chains (templates) combine — additively, synergistically, or as prerequisites — to produce an integrated architectural effect. All T1.5 domain theories are expressed as molecules, but molecules also include system-defined composites that are not established named theories (e.g. M_BEAUTY_COMPRESSION, GOLDILOCKS_PRINCIPLE). Molecules are the primary unit for translating theory into design guidance.
Molecule.relationship_to_T1_5: T1.5 theories are a strict subset of molecules — those with established literature authorship and formal construct definitions. Other molecules are system-generated or emerging composites.

T2.name: CMR Templates (Mechanism Chains)
T2.definition: Specific mechanism pathways encoding: Architectural Feature → Neural/Cognitive Process → Psychological Outcome. Each template specifies from_entity, activity, to_entity, change_produced, parameter_range, evidence_base, and interactions. Templates are the atomic unit of mechanistic explanation. They are composed by molecules and grounded in T1 frameworks.
examples: T1 (Visual Scene Statistics: 1/f spectra → V1 efficient coding → reduced PE)

T3.name: Empirical Beliefs
T3.definition: Lower-level, well-supported empirical beliefs in the Web of Belief. Each T3 belief is a specific, evidence-backed claim about an environment-outcome relationship (e.g. 'ceiling height > 3m increases creative output'). Multiple articles can support the same T3 belief, giving it higher entrenchment. T3 beliefs are the ground-level evidence that templates predict and domain theories organise.
T3.relationship_to_T2: T3 beliefs provide empirical support for T2 template predictions. A template predicts a class of effects; T3 beliefs are the individual instantiations observed in specific studies.
examples: 'Nature views reduce cortisol by 15-20% within 10 min' (supported by 12 articles)
'Curved contours preferred over angular at 65-75% rate' (supported by 8 articles)

causal_direction: T1 explains → T2 specifies → Molecules compose → T1.5 organises → T3 provides evidence
key_principle: Higher tiers are MORE explanatory but LESS specific. Lower tiers are MORE specific but LESS explanatory. The system achieves both depth and breadth by linking all levels.
